Management Plan
2026
Directorate-General for Communication
1

PART 1. Introduction
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general objectives.
This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the actions of
all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for 2025-
2029 in Management plan 2025. This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives and
indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning and
reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what Directorate-General for Communication (DG COMM)
intends to deliver this year to contribute to these multiannual objectives (part 2). It also describes
how DG COMM will contribute to the common objective of building a modern and sustainable
public administration (part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets are presented
in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG COMM.
3

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
As domain leader for external communication, DG COMM will develop integrated communication
strategies, plans and products to support the President and the College of Commissioners. It will
also develop a long-term communication strategy for the Commission. DG COMM ensures timely
political and media insight at both national and local level and promotes information integrity
and builds resilience against information manipulation and disinformation.
DG COMM will also communicate the Commission’s priorities, policies and initiatives, through
campaigns, strategic actions and communication products that highlight the EU's achievements
and benefits for European citizens. These efforts include engaging young people through evolving
digital and social media strategies, collaboration with content creators and organisations
interested in EU initiatives.
In 2026, DG COMM will continue to facilitate citizen engagement and participation in EU
policymaking through the European Citizens’ Panels, European Citizens Platform and support
networks like EUROPE DIRECT. Its visitor services will continue providing interactive educational
experiences, enhancing citizens' understanding of EU policies and their impact.
Overall, DG COMM aligns its activities with the Commission's objectives of fostering a modern,
high-performing, and sustainable EU, upholding democratic values, and ensuring citizen
engagement in policymaking through consistent messaging and reliable communication
channels. This strategic communication framework aims to strengthen the bond between the EU
and its citizens, encouraging a collaborative and informed European community.
While DG COMM does not have any acquis under its remit, therefore no stress testing can be
expected on key simplification and implementation activities for 2026.
The performance tables with key outputs their indicators and targets described below are shown
in Annex 1.
5

General objective 8: A modern, high-performing and
sustainable European Commission
The key outputs described below will contribute to reaching the specific objectives 8.1 and 8.2
set out in DG COMM’s strategic outlook and to Commission’s general objective ‘A modern, high-
performing and sustainable European Commission’ by providing the President and the College
with high quality communication products, services and advice. This includes developing multi-
platform communication products and ensuring consistent and impactful messaging on policy
priorities and benefits for citizens.
Specific objective 8.1: DG COMM provides the President and the College with high-
quality communication products, services and advice, including information on
developments at national and local levels relevant for the shaping of Commission
initiatives.
In 2026, DG COMM remains committed to delivering cutting-edge and integrated
communication and political insight services to the President and the College of
Commissioners. As part of its comprehensive support, it offers around-the-clock services,
including advanced graphic and editorial production, innovative outreach materials, digital
communication and immersive multimedia content. DG COMM continues to ensure that
communication services and products are seamlessly aligned with the evolving needs and
political landscape.
The Spokesperson's Service (SPP) will deliver essential news and developments about
Commission policies and initiatives to press and media outlets. This includes preparing press
materials, the midday press briefings, press events, and coordinating op-eds by Members of the
College in Member States, in collaboration with Cabinet communication advisers, DG COMM
teams, and European Commission Representations in Member States (Representations).
In 2026, DG COMM will continue enhancing strategic and integrated communication
planning across the Commission by coordinating, delivering and implementing high-quality,
timely communication strategies and plans on priority College initiatives and overarching themes,
ensuring coherent narratives and alignment with the President’s Political Guidelines and the
Commission Work Programme.
In 2026, DG COMM will continue to prepare integrated reports on key priority themes and
political developments for the President and the College with insight and advice combining
political reporting, media and social media analysis, vulnerabilities and public opinion. DG COMM
will also strengthen the Commission’s knowledge of youth audiences to optimise the design,
targeting and impact of communication and outreach activities towards young people. This
includes identifying and promoting innovative communication practices and monitoring emerging
trends in youth communication. The involvement of young people and their representatives will
be strengthened through participatory activities and feedback mechanisms, so that
communication efforts are informed by young people’s views.
In 2026, DG COMM will continue to closely monitor and analyse citizens' views on key
European topics through its Standard Eurobarometer surveys. Complementing these efforts,
6

DG COMM will conduct ad-hoc surveys focussed on current challenges and priorities. Additionally,
a series of thematic surveys comprising 12 Special and 15 Flash surveys are planned to cover
diverse areas such as justice, rights and values, in cooperation with the responsible services.
Beyond these surveys, DG COMM is committed to monitoring and reporting on other relevant
opinion polls to ensure a comprehensive understanding of public opinion across a range of issues.
DG COMM will continue to monitor issues related to foreign information manipulation,
and interference (FIMI) and disinformation that could impact the EU, its policies, and
institutions. By conducting strategic communication actions, DG COMM will work to understand
and anticipate vulnerabilities that may affect how EU policies are perceived. Timely and effective
responses to safeguard the integrity and public understanding of the Commission's initiatives,
fostering trust and transparency are part of DG COMMs core deliverables.
DG COMM will support the setting up and functioning of the European Centre for Democratic
Resilience. As announced in the European Democracy Shield communication, the Centre will
primarily work as a dedicated hub for exchange and operational cooperation among EU
institutions and Member States. The Centre will link together existing networks and structures
working on prevention, detection, analysis and response to patterns of threats in the information
space, and work to develop joint approaches, practices and methodologies and exchanging
relevant data and analyses. It will support trainings and capacity-building activities. It could
further advise on common response tools, strategies, standard operating procedures, protocols
or joint exercises.
In addition, the Representations will continue to support the President and the College
in their interactions with Member States. They provide the College and senior management with
country-specific political insights, advice and policy analysis, including reports and briefings, in
collaboration with the Secretariat-General (SG). Representations will also support Members of
the College during the approximatively 700 visits to Member States expected in 2026 by
facilitating contacts and engagement with national, regional and local authorities, the media,
stakeholders and the public beyond the capitals.
When it comes to communication campaigns, DG COMM will continue to develop and implement
cross-channel communication products, campaigns, and activities at both EU and national
levels. These initiatives play a key role in engaging with citizens across Europe and enhancing
their understanding of the EU and its values.
In 2026, DG COMM will launch the 'Democracy Campaign' targeted at 18–30-year-olds, with
a specific emphasis on including those who feel 'left behind'. Alongside this central initiative,
semi-decentralised campaigns adapted to local audiences will focus on the achievements of
the EU budget. These efforts aim to ensure comprehensive outreach and engagement at both
central and local levels.
Additionally, tailored local campaigns will address country-specific opportunities and
challenges, enhancing EU identity and raising awareness and engagement across Member States.
By using approaches relevant to each Member State’s unique context, DG COMM ensures
effective communication and outreach.
DG COMM will also co-develop the campaign on the quality of European food. alongside the
Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development (DG AGRI), ensuring a strategic
7

partnership in promoting European agricultural products.
Throughout 2026, the Representations will organise events for stakeholders, multipliers, the
media and the public, aligning with both European and local communication objectives. These
events will be adapted to the local media landscape and tailored to meet specific local needs.
Specific objective 8.2: DG COMM steers Commission services to develop
communication activities and products consistent and coherent with its
communication strategy and objectives, including through integrated
communication planning on Commission priorities.
As domain leader in external communication, in 2026 DG COMM will continue developing its long-
term horizontal communication strategy framework to define a comprehensive and shared
strategic approach to external communication of the Commission, reinforcing coherence,
efficiency and impact.
DG COMM will continue to contribute to enhancing the strategic alignment of
communication actions and corporate communication governance in the Commission. This
will be done through the Corporate Communication Steering Committee and the External
Communication Network, continuous collaboration with Commission policy services,
prioritising Commission-wide communication initiatives. It will also boost its monitoring
through an improved IT tool facilitating the information flow inside the Commission.
DG COMM plays a pivotal role in steering communication campaigns designed and developed by
other Commission services, including to approximately 30 campaigns that undergo enhanced
monitoring under the ‘Right of Consent’ procedure.
Additionally, DG COMM is committed to driving the strategic development and coordination
of youth-focused communication and outreach activities within the Commission. The
integration of the youth dimension into these initiatives aims to deliver coherent and tailored
messaging that resonates with young audiences and aligns with the Commission's corporate
priorities.
Through the Network against disinformation, DG COMM plays a key role in steering work linked
to situational awareness and resilience building as well as in supporting and advising on relevant
thematic issues.
In the area of social media, the focus in 2026 will be on enhancing the strategic and creative
branding of the Commission’s social media presence by streamlining activities to ensure
more effective and targeted outreach. This involves addressing new audience segments through
tailored accounts and channels and ensuring complementarity across platforms. Additionally, the
impact of the Commission's flagship accounts will be increased through increased editorial
coordination, with a strengthened creative touch. Utilising data-driven audience segmentation
and performance analytics will maximise reach and impact.
The professionalisation of the Commission Services and Representations’ social media presence
through the Social Media Network will further boost EU-wide information dissemination with
coherent branding and editorial priorities
8

A new strategy will be implemented to shape the Commission’s audiovisual presence
on YouTube and foster increased engagement. Increased efforts to design data-driven
target groups and channels, will inform new adapted formats for content including for news,
explainers, educational or promotional material. Efforts will be made to reach unengaged
audiences, while synchronising with other social media platforms and production processes,
including local and multilingual adaptation efforts supported by Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools.
In 2026 the content creators’ programme will be further developed into a structural
element across various communication activities. Their involvement in major political events and
priorities will be strengthened to multiply reach and impact. Study visits, webinars, and other
training and engagement opportunities will be increased to keep content creators informed and
engaged, while striving to increase the numbers and diversity of influencers in collaboration with
Representations and Commission Services.
DG COMM will adapt the Commission’s web presence to the opportunities and challenges of
the internet in the age of widespread use of AI systems for information retrieval. DG COMM will
also continue to enhance accessibility and multilingualism across the Commission’s websites,
and the web presence will be consolidated by focusing on strategic, high-quality editorial content
and clearer user journeys.
To further enrich the web experience, DG COMM will develop narrative-driven content such as
storytelling and explainers on politically important themes, alongside topical content linked to
significant developments.
In 2026, DG COMM will enhance its role in interservice coordination and interinstitutional
communication governance by actively participating in consultations, offering strategic
communication insights on initiatives, and strengthening cooperation with EU institutions, bodies
and agencies to ensure aligned communication actions and coherent messaging.
General objective 5: Protecting our democracy, upholding our
values
The key outputs described below will contribute to reaching the specific objective 5.1 set out in
DG COMM’s strategic outlook and to the Commission’s general objective ‘Protecting our
democracy, upholding our values’, mainly by engaging with citizens, also in partnership with
national and local authorities, and fostering their participation in the design of EU policies.
Specific objective 5.1: DG COMM steers the Commission’s engagement with citizens.
It develops citizens’ engagement activities, also in partnership with national and
local authorities, and fosters citizens’ participation in the design of EU policies.
In 2026, DG COMM will sustain its efforts to integrate citizen participation across the Commission
by organising two European Citizens’ Panels, aimed at contributing the implementation of the
Preparedness Strategy and the European Democracy Shield.
DG COMM will also actively contribute to the third pillar of the European Democracy Shield,
notably to boosting societal resilience and citizens’ engagement.
9

Alongside these initiatives, DG COMM will continue to facilitate online participatory debates
through the Citizens’ Engagement Platform, which aims to broaden the reach of the
European Citizens’ Panels and Youth Policy Dialogues. This online platform seeks to create
synergies with other elements of the Have Your Say Portal, enhancing the impact and inclusivity
of citizen interactions with the Commission's activities and policies.
In close cooperation with the Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture
(DG EAC), DG COMM will provide strategic direction for youth engagement in high-level
meetings, such as the Youth Policy Dialogues and the President’s Youth Advisory Board. DG COMM
will also advise the Commission Services on bottom-up activities that involve co-creation of
communication assets and events with young people and/or their representatives.
The Commission’s visitor services managed by DG COMM provide engaging and educational
experiences geared to citizens deeper understanding of the Commission’s activities and policies.
This includes Experience Europe and the Visitors’ Centre in Brussels. In 2026, the Commission will
start modernising its offer and enhance the visitors’ experience, making it more user-centric and
integrated. Additionally, DG COMM will continue its support for the Europa Experience exhibitions
centers in the Member States, in close cooperation with the European Parliament.
In 2026, DG COMM will launch the new generation of EUROPE DIRECT Centres focusing on
organising events to foster citizen engagement and enhance awareness of EU policies. The
EUROPE DIRECT Contact Centre (EDCC) will continue to serve as a key entry point of contact
for citizens, offering personalised responses to inquiries related to the EU through phone, email,
and chat services, available in all 24 official languages along with Ukrainian and Russian.
DG COMM will contribute to the work of the Centre for Democratic Resilience, by facilitating a
consolidated whole-of-society response to increase awareness, promote citizenship engagement
and build resilience to Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) and
disinformation.
DG COMM will further foster direct engagement with citizens by organising the Commission Open
Day in Brussels, a key event coinciding with the Europe Day celebrations centred around the
Commission's priorities.
10

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to
acceptable levels through cost-effective controls.
DG COMM has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an
ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
The related performance tables with their indicators and targets are shown in Annex 2 to this
plan.
A. Human resource management
In 2026, to support efficiency and co-creation across the services, DG COMM will continually
evaluate its recently reorganised structure, refine the flexible workflows that have been
developed in its wake, use agile transversal project teams on key policy communication
campaigns and continue supporting the digital upskilling of its staff and management, in
particular on the use of collaborative tools and on the uptake of Artificial Intelligence
(AI) tools. Among other refinements, the 2025 reorganisation led to the creation of a dedicated
unit for strategy, coordination & governance in the external communications domain, which will
help DG COMM further enhance its leadership in the field.
As part of an active change management and to support staff engagement and well-being,
DG COMM will also maintain its active internal communication and staff mobility actions.
DG COMM will continue to organise hybrid, all-staff ‘townhall’ meetings at least twice a year,
accompanied by other monthly opportunities for knowledge-sharing and discussion, for both staff
management, in the form of ‘KnowledgeCOMM’ sessions, ‘COMM Capsules’ and middle
management meetings, in addition to offering a weekly online senior management meeting
debrief to foster staff engagement in the service. These measures will be flanked by other
communication actions to raise awareness of staff mobility initiatives, such as the annual call
for Representation-based contract agents to consider reassignment to other Representations.
Furthermore, DG COMM will continue to be actively involved in the large-scale review, focusing
in particular on the overall delivery of Commission’s communication, outreach and engagement
and on presence in Member States and the role of Representations.
The key indicators on HR management for DG COMM on 1 October 2025 were: 55.8% of
managers in DG COMM were female, with 56.3% in middle management and 54.5% in senior
management, thereby contributing to the Commission’s gender balance targets at corporate
level. Going forward, as a net contributor to the corporate Commission gender balance target for
females in middle management, DG COMM aims to maintain the value around 50%.
11

B. Digital transformation and data management
Digital transformation
Abiding by the Digital Transformation Strategy, DG COMM is prioritising its digital transformation
as part of the Digital Transformation Strategy, focusing on developing digital skills and
embracing emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) where appropriate. This
transformation is supported by the Learning and Development Strategy. Business-driven digital
transformation will progress with AI tools, including a virtual assistant and voice-to-text solutions
as well as using AI for data analysis and visualisation, applied for instance to communication
performance data. AI will also be leveraged for business process automation and improving
knowledge-sharing capabilities, aligning with the Commission's goals for efficient internal
operations and public service delivery. In line with EC Corporate IT Governance, DG COMM will
ensure that the use and development of AI systems will follow internal governance and
guidelines, and reuse as much as possible corporate building blocks. To ensure a seamless digital
environment, DG COMM will be implementing its new, more focussed and streamlined approach
to local IT governance aiming for a deeper and broader participation of business stakeholders,
as well as increased efficiency of its IT projects. This includes ensuring IT and security compliance,
making IT projects easier to manage, and ensuring solutions are scalable and reusable. DG COMM
will be working towards DIGIT’s multiannual priority of cloud migration and it will be implementing
system security updates while preparing for the modernisation and further streamlining of its
local IT systems (replacing obsolete tools with more agile and user-friendly ones and further
integrating AI into DG COMM workflows). It will work with DIGIT on ensuring high-level security
of the digital infrastructure and train staff for digital risks to enhance cybersecurity awareness.
Data management
DG COMM continues to leverage the full potential of its data assets to improve evidence-based
decision-making through the DG COMM Management Knowledge Platform. In 2025, the
Platform's scope and functionality were refined, leveraging a comprehensive 'Data Lake' to
consolidate data assets. 2026 will see further improvements in the Platform to visualise the
impacts of digital and physical external communication activities. In parallel, the platform use by
the staff and management will be actively promoted.
The maturity level in implementing corporate data policies will continue at the current level of
‘developing’ for 2026 across all four key areas of data management, ownership and
responsibilities, data quality, and data skills in DG COMM. The successful ongoing development
and deployment of the DG COMM Management Knowledge Platform has is not only consolidating
DG COMM’s data assets in a “Data Lake” but has highlighted the need for a more structured
approach to DG COMM’s data management and data culture more generally. FAIRness principles
are therefore a key basis for fostering the use of this Platform, by making its data Findable,
Accessible, Interoperable & Reusable. To achieve this, DG COMM will continue to map and
catalogue DG COMM data assets and their attributes, which will also help ensure that data roles
are properly identified, recorded and reported. Some DG COMM data assets are reported in the
EC Data Catalogue, but coverage is sometimes incomplete or inconsistent. These inconsistencies
will be addressed in 2026. In the area of data skills, DG COMM will continue its internal
communication efforts to raise general skill levels of its staff in the areas of AI and use of the
collaborative tools in Microsoft’s M365 suite of software.
12

DG COMM remains committed to leading by example in the field of data protection in
accordance with Commission’s legal obligation and political commitment. It will continue
conducting biennial reviews of public records of processing operations to ensure that the
information is accurate, up-to-date and transparent. This will minimise the risks from the
processing of personal data. DG COMM will continue investing in raising awareness through
general and specialised training for staff at Headquarters and Representations.
The percentage of staff trained on data protection compliance combined with the percentage of
public records of processing operations reviewed within the last two years is 76.95 (1), end 2025.
C. Sound financial management
DG COMM will perform several ex-post controls on a sample of financial transactions in given
entities to highlight potential recurrent issues, which may require mitigating actions across
headquarters and in the Representations. Based on concrete operational needs of DG COMM, in
2026, it will also perform cross-cutting thematic ex-post controls (of a similar type as the 2024
control of consumption of ceilings of Framework Contracts) and it will continue to closely monitor
the financial and procurement procedures to support further rationalisation actions. This is
facilitated by the centralisation of procurement activities in DG COMM and the establishment of
a virtual procurement team among Representations. DG COMM will continue supporting the two
communities of practice for its financial actors in Headquarters and in the Representations, who
will regularly meet to stay updated on financial developments and practices. Identified sub-
groups will receive tailored refreshment and training courses to meet their specific needs.
D. Fraud risk management
With its revised Anti-Fraud Strategy adopted at the end of 2025, DG COMM will contribute to the
implementation of the Commission anti-fraud strategy (CAFS) action plan. Based on a thorough
analysis of the inherent risks in DG COMM – e.g. a high number of actors in Headquarters and
the Representations, potential conflicts of interest, small and specialised markets of suppliers –
DG COMM’s Anti-Fraud Strategy focuses on two key objectives: to increase anti-fraud awareness
and to ensure the detection of fraud. In this context, it will maintain its awareness raising and
information efforts on fraud prevention in-house and in collaboration with European Anti-Fraud
Office (OLAF) and/or Investigation and Disciplinary Office (HR-IDOC) with at least 2 tailored
training sessions on ethics and anti-fraud per year. Moreover, DG COMM will streamline its fraud
detection measures through ex-ante / ex-post controls with a systematic verification of red flags
and a target of less than 5% of transactions checked containing ‘red flags”. Besides, data
analytics on procurement will complement fraud detection. The non-compliance or exception
events (internal control principle 12) related to the red flags detected by ex-ante/ex-post controls
will be closely followed up.
A systematic verification of red flag indicators will be performed to detect potential fraudulent
behaviour in both ex-ante and ex-post controls. The non-compliance or exception events (internal

For the indicator on fraud risk management, the implementation of DG COMM actions under its
previous anti-fraud strategy reached 100% early 2025. The revised Anti-Fraud Strategy foresees
100% of due actions implemented each year.
E. Sound environmental management
In 2026, DG COMM continues to enhance environmental sustainability by minimising mobility
emissions, digitalising workflows, and fostering staff engagement. These initiatives are in keeping
with the Greening the Commission Communication, laying a solid foundation for upcoming
efforts. By promoting sustainable mobility and expanding the use of videoconferencing, travel
emissions will be further curtailed. Additionally, three awareness actions will be implemented to
reduce emissions from staff activities, aiming to further decrease individual carbon footprints. A
strategic decision has been made to close DG COMM buildings for 17 working days, thus
significantly reducing energy consumption and emissions during this period. The emphasis will
be on ensuring that events are environmentally friendly through the use of digital materials,
waste reduction strategies, and eco-conscious catering options. This methodology reinforces
DG COMM's commitment to aligning with the Commission's environmental objectives.
For the indicator on sound environmental management, DG COMM’s staff travel emissions was
343 tons of CO2 equivalent end 2025 (the baseline end 2019 was 697 tons of CO2 equivalent).
